report_name: 'SilkParasite' Espionage Campaign Targets Central Asian Governments

threat_actors.name: SilkParasite Group
threat_actors.description: A China-nexus cyberespionage group responsible for the SilkParasite campaign. This actor targets government entities in Central Asia to gather intelligence on economic matters, using a custom arsenal of RATs.
threat_actors.goals: Long-term espionage to gather intelligence on economic matters from Central Asian governments.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: Used for initial access by sending spear-phishing emails with password-protected RAR archives containing malicious Microsoft Office documents.

attack_patterns.name: DLL Side-Loading
attack_patterns.description: A legitimate application is used to load a malicious DLL, which executes the malware payload as part of the infection chain.

attack_patterns.name: Web Protocols
attack_patterns.description: DriveSilkRAT uses the Google Drive API for C2 communications, which leverages standard web protocols (HTTPS) to blend in with legitimate traffic.

attack_patterns.name: Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The legitimate Google Drive cloud service was abused for command and control to download new plugins and receive commands.

attack_patterns.name: Input Capture
attack_patterns.description: The deployed RATs have keylogging capabilities to steal credentials and other sensitive information.

attack_patterns.name: Screen Capture
attack_patterns.description: The deployed RATs can capture screenshots to monitor victim activity and gather intelligence.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The RATs exfiltrate gathered intelligence, such as files and captured data, through their established command and control channels.

malware.name: DriveSilkRAT
malware.description: A previously undocumented Remote Access Trojan that uses the Google Drive API for command and control, allowing it to download plugins and receive commands.

malware.name: CookiETagRAT
malware.description: A previously undocumented Remote Access Trojan used in the SilkParasite campaign.

malware.name: NomadRAT
malware.description: A previously undocumented Remote Access Trojan used in the SilkParasite campaign.

malware.name: GoginRAT
malware.description: A previously undocumented Remote Access Trojan used in the SilkParasite campaign.

malware.name: NodeEdgeRAT
malware.description: A previously undocumented Remote Access Trojan used in the SilkParasite campaign.

malware.name: ShadowPad
malware.description: A known China-nexus toolset whose characteristics were observed in the malware used in the SilkParasite campaign.

malware.name: Deed RAT
malware.description: A known China-nexus toolset linked to the malware used in the SilkParasite campaign.

tools.name: Google Drive
tools.description: Legitimate cloud storage service abused by DriveSilkRAT for command and control communications to evade detection.

campaigns.name: SilkParasite
campaigns.description: A cyberespionage campaign active since October 2025, attributed to a China-nexus actor, targeting government entities in Central Asia with a custom arsenal of RATs.
campaigns.objective: Long-term espionage to gather intelligence on economic matters.

identities.name: Central Asian Government Entities
identities.description: Government organizations in Central Asia involved in economic policy and decision-making, targeted by the SilkParasite campaign.

infrastructure.name: Google Drive C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Google Drive was used by DriveSilkRAT to host commands and download new plugins, blending C2 traffic with legitimate cloud service activity.

indicators.name: SilkParasite Google Drive C2 Traffic
indicators.pattern:
title: SilkParasite Google Drive C2 Traffic
id: 2b1a8c7d-3e4f-4a9b-8c1d-9e8f7a6b5c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections to Google Drive API endpoints from non-browser processes, which could indicate the use of Google Drive for C2 communications as seen with DriveSilkRAT.
references:
  - https://industrialcyber.co/cisa/bitdefender-traces-silkparasite-cyberespionage-campaign-across-central-asia-to-seven-rat-families-china-nexus-tooling/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
tags:
  - attack.t1102
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - 'drive.google.com'
      - 'googleapis.com'
    Initiated: true
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects network traffic to Google Drive APIs from non-browser applications, a TTP used by DriveSilkRAT for C2.

indicators.name: SilkParasite DLL Side-Loading with Rundll32
indicators.pattern:
title: SilkParasite DLL Side-Loading with Rundll32
id: 5d9c0b3a-1e8f-4b7c-9a6d-2e3f4a5b6c7d
status: experimental
description: Detects rundll32.exe executing a DLL from a non-standard directory, a TTP associated with the SilkParasite campaign.
references:
  - https://industrialcyber.co/cisa/bitdefender-traces-silkparasite-cyberespionage-campaign-across-central-asia-to-seven-rat-families-china-nexus-tooling/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
tags:
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1218.011
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '.dll'
  filter:
    CommandLine|startswith:
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\'
      - '"C:\Windows\System32\'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects the use of rundll32.exe to execute a malicious DLL, a technique used for execution in the SilkParasite campaign.

indicators.name: Suspicious Process Spawn from MS Office
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Process Spawn from MS Office Application
id: 8e4f1a9b-7c6d-4b5a-8d3e-1f2a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious child processes spawning from Microsoft Office applications, which may indicate malicious macro execution or exploitation as seen in the SilkParasite campaign's initial access phase.
references:
  - https://industrialcyber.co/cisa/bitdefender-traces-silkparasite-cyberespionage-campaign-across-central-asia-to-seven-rat-families-china-nexus-tooling/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
tags:
  - attack.t1566.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\WINWORD.EXE'
      - '\EXCEL.EXE'
      - '\POWERPNT.EXE'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\splwow64.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\WINWORD.EXE'
      - '\EXCEL.EXE'
      - '\POWERPNT.EXE'
      - '\Microsoft.Mashup.Container.NetFX40.exe'
      - '\Microsoft.Mashup.Container.NetFX45.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects unusual processes spawning from Microsoft Office applications, a potential indicator of initial access via a malicious document.

relationships.source_name: Suspicious Process Spawn from MS Office
